messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 — GPU pool gpool-prod-eu: queue length > 1200, avg latency spike 4x, autoscaler hit max_replicas. Paging Maya. https://observability.redwood/gpool/gpool-prod-eu :rotating_light:
Maya (sre-oncall): on it. grabbing current graphs and logs. is this correlated with any recent deploys?
Dan (runtime): yes, we rolled model v5.3.2 to canary in eu region ~10m ago. patch changed context handling to preserve larger kv-entries by default.
Carla (infra): autoscaler reports "scale_limit_reached" and several scale attempts failed due to gpu-quota-per-tenant hard cap (cfg:max_replicas=12). current replicas=12, queue=1300.
Maya (sre-oncall): ok, immediate mitigation proposals: 1) route traffic for this model to a fallback variant (v5.2.x) 2) raise max_replicas temporarily if quota allow 3) apply token/context cap per-request. Which is fastest?
Dan (runtime): fastest is routing to fallback. apply a route override to pin requests matching model:v5.3.2 to model:v5.2. We have a rollout feature flag.
Maya (sre-oncall): Carla, can infra do a manual bump of pool size while we route? If quota prevents, we should at least reduce incoming load.
Carla (infra): quota team says we have 2 spare GPUs in eu region but they'd require approval for permanent bump. I can add 2 GPUs to the pool for 30m now. doing it.
infra-bot: Executing pool resize: gcloud compute instances resize --add-gpus 2 --zone europe-west1-b 
infra-bot: Resize succeeded. new replicas target=14. autoscaler notified.
Maya (sre-oncall): Dan, start route override now. Share command.
Dan (runtime): running route change:

```
POST https://api.redwood.internal/routing/overrides
{
  "match": {"model":"v5.3.2", "region":"eu"},
  "route_to": "model:v5.2.x",
  "ttl": 1800
}
```

Dan (runtime): override applied. returning traffic to v5.2.x for eu.
James (support): any customer impact? I have a ticket from a few enterprise customers reporting slower responses for chat endpoints. Need ETA to update them.
Maya (sre-oncall): initial impact window started ~2067891228. Estimated affected requests ~8% of total EU traffic, primarily long-context sessions. We should tell customers: degraded latencies and increased error retries during 2067891228-?.
Olivia (pm): flagging that v5.3.2 was rolled to canary then promoted yesterday. We need short customer note: temporary routing to stable (v5.2.x) while we investigate. James, draft a brief status update I can review.
James (support): drafting now: "We’ve routed traffic to a stable model variant in EU after a performance regression in a recent model patch. Some requests experienced increased latency and retry errors. We’re mitigating and will follow up with root cause. No data loss."
Dan (runtime): quick root-cause notes: v5.3.2 increases default kv-cache retention and keeps more context in memory which increased per-request memory and GPU time, amplifying batching inefficiency. Also batching heuristic didn't adapt to longer sequences, so throughput per GPU dropped markedly.
Maya (sre-oncall): logs show KV-cache & attention memory accounting suddenly doubled for long-session requests. snippet from runtime logs: 

```
[2067891227] model=v5.3.2 seq=8192 kv_mem=1.9GB tokens/sec=48 batch_pending=23
[2067891230] autoscaler: attempted_scale +2 -> failed (quota cap)
```

Carla (infra): autoscaler policy had a safety cap to avoid noisy autoscaling for new variants; that policy prevented quicker scale beyond 12. We need policy tweak to allow emergency scale for verified canaries.
Dan (runtime): agree. we'll also add a temporary heuristic to clamp sequence length per request for v5.3.2: max_context=4096 by config until we fix kernel/kv behavior.
Maya (sre-oncall): Dan, apply clamp now and push patch.
Dan (runtime): applying patch: 

```
PATCH /runtime/config
- model.v5.3.2.max_context = 8192
+ model.v5.3.2.max_context = 4096
```

Dan (runtime): patch applied and hot-reloaded. monitoring token rates...
Maya (sre-oncall): queue dropping — current queue 300, latency trending down. autoscaler scaled to 14 and stabilized.
infra-bot: autoscaler event: scaled +2 -> replicas=14 (manual/quota bump)
Carla (infra): open follow-up: petition quota team for EU permanent increase and change autoscaler policy to allow emergency buffer for canary spikes. I’ll file infra ticket INF-4521.
Olivia (pm): plan for next steps: 1) rollback v5.3.2 promotion and mark canary as blocked until perf fixes 2) add e2e perf tests for long-context on CI 3) update rollout checklist to include autoscale policy check.
James (support): posted customer note to the affected enterprise tickets and status page update. customers acknowledged, want RCA and ETA for permanent fix.
Maya (sre-oncall): current status: mitigations in place, traffic routed to stable, context clamp applied, temporary capacity added. Impact isolated. I'll hand off to next oncall in 4h for monitoring and RCA drive.
Olivia (pm): I'll schedule a triage meeting in 1h with runtime/infra/research to scope root cause and timeline.
Dan (runtime): immediate follow-ups: investigate batching heuristic and kv retention policy, reproduce locally with long-context harness.
Carla (infra): infra follow-ups: INF-4521 (quota + autoscaler policy), ensure resize runbook includes emergency steps.
Maya (sre-oncall): thanks all. saving logs and metrics to incident folder: https://observability.redwood/incidents/2067891234. handing off to next oncall @dan-pager at 2067891269. :white_check_mark:
